title: How to Track GoHighLevel Forms in GTM, Tested on a Live Form
intro:
I wrote this post, published it, and then took it down. The listener had only passed simulated tests, and that isn't enough for a guide you might follow on a client's site.

So I found a live page built on GoHighLevel and put a real, clearly labelled test lead through its native form. The lead went through and the listener caught it, with the name, email, phone and ZIP intact. The form's validation error, though, didn't fire ghl_form_failed. That was a bug in my listener, and I fixed it and retested it on the same form.

Here's how to install it, with the names removed.
tldr: Add one free Custom HTML tag and trigger on ghl_form_success. On a native GoHighLevel form it caught a real lead with full contact data, and it also accepts iframe messages from GoHighLevel domains. The iframe path hasn't been tested on a live form yet, so test yours before you rely on it.
sections: A form and a calendar look alike from outside

Here's what the listener accepts, and what it ignores:

Message or stateResult
Lead payload from leadconnectorhq.com, msgsndr.com or gohighlevel.com, with an email, phone or nameghl_form_success, method postmessage
Booking, appointment or calendar messageIgnored
Same payload from any other origin, or not from a GoHighLevel iframe on the pageIgnored
Inline form removed or hidden after submitghl_form_success
Inline form redirects to a same-domain thank-you pageghl_form_success, from stored data
Inline form shows an error after the visitor interactedghl_form_failed

Here's what else is out there:

OptionWhat it doesThe gap
Optizent's guideFree listener for forms and bookings, with separate eventsIts form check looks for an address, customer ID, name and email together, and booking events reuse the last cached inputs
GHL Form Listener on Gumroad$20 GTM setup with Enhanced Conversions data and no thank-you pagePaid, and the page doesn't say how inline forms are handled

If you want booking events too, Optizent's guide covers them and this listener doesn't. I wanted a form event that a booking can't trigger.

1. Download the GTM tag, or get it from GitHub.
  2. In GTM, go to Tags > New > Custom HTML and paste it.
  3. Trigger it on All Pages.
[[img:ghl-listener-tag|An older build, paused in a client container where a universal tag is active. Yours should be active.]]

If the site uses other form tools too, use the universal listener walkthrough instead of stacking tags.

Create a Custom Event trigger on ghl_form_success. This container also splits conversions by hostname, so the main site's leads and landing page leads go to separate conversion actions.

[[img:ghl-trigger|A regex trigger for three form tools, limited to one hostname.]]
Step 3: Send it to GA4 and Google Ads

Add a GA4 Event tag on the trigger. form_platform tells you which kind of embed sent the lead: ghl_iframe for iframes.

[[img:ghl-ga4-tag|Form details only, no contact fields.]]

Put your Google Ads Conversion Tracking tag on the same trigger. Then map ec_email and ec_phone in a User-Provided Data variable, and check the values as shown in the Gravity Forms walkthrough. Iframe payloads carry contact data, so Enhanced Conversions works on both embed types.

[[img:ghl-ec-tag|User-provided data on the success event.]]

Want these in reports? GA4 won't show them until you register each one as a custom dimension. Here's how.

1. In Preview, load the page and expect ec_tracker_initialized.
  2. Submit a labelled test lead. Use a valid phone format, because GoHighLevel rejected our 555-555 test number. Expect one ghl_form_success, and check ec_detection_method and the ec_* values.
  3. If the page has a calendar, book a test slot. No ghl_form_success should fire.
  4. Submit with a required field empty. Expect ghl_form_failed on a native form.
  5. If nothing fires, set debug: true. The console says why each message was ignored.

Then remove old click and thank-you triggers, or each lead counts twice.

• Native form: on a live page in November 2026, a labelled test lead fired one ghl_form_success through pagehide, because the form redirects to a thank-you page. It carried the normalised email and phone, first and last name, ZIP, form ID and button text.
  • Failed event: on that form, an empty required field now fires ghl_form_failed. I didn't test a visitor fixing the error and resubmitting on a live form.
  • Tags: the listener ran in my browser with GTM cut off, so the lead wouldn't reach the client's reports. On a redirecting form the event fires as the page unloads, so check GA4 Realtime and Google Ads after your own test.
  • Iframe embeds: tested in Chrome with simulated messages only, not a live form. GoHighLevel doesn't document this message and could change it. debug: true shows why each message was ignored.
  • No validation failures for iframes, because the parent page can't see them.
  • Some forms only look like GoHighLevel. One site loaded a GoHighLevel iframe, but its visible form was its own. If you see gtm.formSubmit and no listener event, check whose form it is.
closing: If you'd rather have this installed and checked for you, I can help.

seo.card: A real test lead through a live GoHighLevel form, the bug it exposed, and the GTM setup that catches leads with full contact data.
